mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office / national issuing authority of the UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Samoa is a contracting party; for non-Hague jurisdictions, consular legalization at the nearest Samoan diplomatic mission / consulate)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or banking institution in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory onboarding screening of all directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Consolidated List, and Samoa's domestic FIU watchlist. PEP identification is conducted per FATF standards with enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates. Registered agents must complete customer due diligence before engagement, re-screen every 12 months or upon any material change, and file suspicious transaction and cash threshold reports with the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit under the AML/CFT Act 2018.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Companies Office / Registrar of International Companies; all name reservation submissions, extensions, and registrations must be filed through a MCIL-licensed Registered Agent (no direct public e-filing is available for International Companies).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory name of an International Company must be expressed in Latin (Roman) alphabetical characters. Non-Roman scripts, including Chinese characters, are not accepted as the registered statutory name. A Chinese or other non-Roman business name may only be recorded as an unregistered trade alias / trademark in the agent's internal records, provided the statutory name carries a Registrar-approved romanized equivalent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The licensed registered agent may request a single 30-day extension of a name reservation in writing prior to expiry. Upon rejection, the applicant may either (i) resubmit an alternative name through the registered agent, or (ii) file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 business days of the rejection notice. A further appeal may be lodged with the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 30 days of the Registrar's decision, and the Minister's determination is subject to judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable. The International Companies Act 1987 requires a physical registered office in Samoa and a licensed registered agent; the registered office may lawfully be the address of the licensed agent. No physical manufacturing, warehousing, or commercial premises in Samoa are required for this low-risk ISIC 3240 polyresin statue operation, which is conducted outside Samoa.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated 5%–10% probability of an unannounced Registrar or FIU physical inspection within the first three years of operation, absent any AML/CFT triggering event, sanctions match, PEP designation, adverse media, or irregular transaction flow routed through Samoan payment infrastructure.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), ss. 4-12 (incorporation and effect of registration), s. 24 (registered office and registered agent), ss. 46-58 (directors, secretary and corporate administration); International Companies Regulations 1997.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registrar of International Companies, Apia, Samoa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 (Application for Registration as an International Company) together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association and required consents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the International Companies Act 1987. The Company may be registered with one or more shares of no par value. No escrowed capital contribution or pre-determined authorized share capital threshold is required at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers to the Memorandum and Articles of Association of [●] (the Company) do hereby adopt [address, Apia, Samoa] as the registered office of the Company and appoint [●] as first director. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the initial share capital of the Company be divided into [●] shares of no par value, and the subscription in respect of [●] shares by [●] is ratified, with such shares fully paid for all purposes of the International Companies Act 1987. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [●] is appointed Secretary of the Company, and the corporators are authorised to file all documents and pay all fees to the Samoa International Finance Authority and to execute any ancillary instruments required to complete incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Corporate Services Section, Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed international company name to the SIFA Registry by e-filing or physical lodgment. The name must not conflict with any registered company nor be misleading or undesirable for a tax-exempt international company. Payment of the name reservation fee secures the name for 60 days.
required_dossiers: Notarized passport copy of the proposed incorporator/subscriber
Short written statement describing the intended lawful business (polyresin statue manufacturing and garage kits)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar refuses a name, file a written request for reconsideration supported by a legal opinion within 14 days, or select a new distinctive name and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Execution and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa notary public or Commissioner for Oaths, with final lodgment at SIFA Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association containing the company name, registered office clause, share structure, objects, and powers. Have the incorporator execute the documents before a notary public. Each director and secretary must execute a separate consent to act. The registered agent in Apia must execute an acceptance of appointment.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (original notarized)
Certificate of Good Standing for any corporate director, shareholder or agent (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notarization or authentication irregularity is identified, cure by re-execution and re-notarization; no resubmission fee applies if the corrected set is submitted within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing with SIFA and Payment of Government Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registration Unit, Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 1 together with the notarized Memorandum and Articles, consents, and registered agent acceptance. Pay the official government fee by wire transfer or direct deposit to SIFA's designated account. The application must include a declaration that the company will not carry on business with the public in Samoa except as permitted under the International Companies Act 1987.
required_dossiers: Executed and notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to Act of each director and secretary
Proof of payment of incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA issues a requisition or query, respond within 21 days with the missing document or clarification. A written extension request may be submitted to the Registrar; if unanswered after 21 days the file is deemed abandoned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon full compliance, the Registrar enters the company in the International Companies Register and issues the Certificate of Incorporation. Verify the exact legal name, company registration number, date of incorporation, and share capital details on the certificate.
required_dossiers: Application checklist or acknowledgement from SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For typographical or accidental errors in the Certificate, file a Notice of Rectification under section 108 of the International Companies Act 1987, return the original certificate for cancellation, and request a corrected certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Post-Incorporation Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First director and secretary of the Company, acting through SIFA-registered records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold or circulate a written first board resolution to adopt the registered office, ratify the issue of initial shares, appoint the first director and secretary, approve the form of share certificate, and authorize opening of corporate bank accounts. File the registered office and agent details with SIFA and maintain statutory registers at the registered agent's office in Samoa.
required_dossiers: Minutes or written resolution of the first board of directors
Certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any officer appointment is found procedurally invalid, ratify it by a written resolution of the subscriber or board before filing any subsequent annual return; correction within 30 days avoids late penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Business Licences Division; Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA) of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE); Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence under the Business Licences Act 1998; Development Consent under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004; Workplace Registration under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2011

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B (controlled industrial activity) requiring a Project Brief and Development Consent; a full Environmental Impact Assessment is mandatory if resin casting operations exceed 100 kg/day VOC emissions, involve hazardous waste storage above threshold quantities, or are located within 100 metres of a residential or water catchment area.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with the Samoa National Environmental Water Quality Standards (BOD ≤ 50 mg/L, TSS ≤ 80 mg/L, pH 6-9, and no detectable priority toxic metals). VOC emissions from vacuum casting and resin mixing must be captured through activated carbon and dry particulate filters, with a ventilation discharge VOC limit not exceeding 500 mg/m³. Gelcoat and polyester resin wastes must be classified as hazardous waste and transported to the authorized landfill at Tafaigata under a waste manifest system.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) is required before operation, with specific inspection of resin and styrene storage areas, ignition source separation, emergency egress, and portable fire extinguisher coverage. Structural load inspection by the MCIL Building Inspectorate under the Samoa Building Code is required for the production floor and mezzanine storage. Occupational clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2011 must include indoor air monitoring for styrene, a respirator and PPE program, chemical safety data sheet registers, emergency response training, and fire drill documentation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Revenue, Government of Samoa (MoR) is the competent tax and customs administration (official portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws). The Samoa Customs Service operates within the MoR and processes all goods declarations through the ASYCUDA World electronic system. The Registrar of International Companies, part of the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), administers International Company incorporation, licensing, and annual franchise fees. The Central Bank of Samoa administers exchange-control and foreign-currency repatriation rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Samoa International Company (IC): (1) file the charter/statutory documents with the Registrar of International Companies and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation, maintaining a Samoa registered office and registered agent; (2) for the IC's offshore business, no income tax or VAGST registration is required because the entity is tax-exempt; (3) if a Samoan bank account, local contracting, or counterparty due diligence requires a number, the IC files the MoR standard TIN application together with the Certificate of Incorporation, certificate of incumbency, register of directors and shareholders, beneficial-ownership declaration, and a statutory declaration confirming no business with Samoa residents, no Samoan-source income, and no Samoan landholding; (4) the MoR issues a TIN or, upon request, a letter confirming tax-exempt status, typically within 5-10 business days. Any entity carrying on a taxable Samoan activity rather than offshore business must register for income tax and VAGST before commencing that activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone. Under the International Companies Act 2012, the IC is a non-resident limited company and is exempt from income tax, capital gains tax, VAGST, stamp duty, estate duty, gift duty, and all other Samoan taxes; it files no Samoan income tax or VAGST returns for offshore business and pays only the fixed annual government franchise fee. Ordinary resident Samoa companies are taxable on worldwide income at the standard corporate rate of 27%, with a legislated multi-year phase-down toward 9%.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no US-style check-the-box regime. The IC may: (a) elect by special resolution to convert to a domestic company under the Companies Act 2001, thereby exiting the tax-exempt zone and becoming subject to full income tax and VAGST registration, or a domestic company may convert into an IC if eligible; (b) elect to continue (redomicile) out of Samoa or receive a foreign company by continuation into Samoa; (c) rely on entity-classification elections made in the foreign parent jurisdiction (e.g., U.S. Form 8832), although Samoa's Income Tax Act 2015 general anti-avoidance, CFC, transfer-pricing, and substance-over-form rules may re-characterize hybrid mismatches or conduit arrangements; no express hybrid-mismatch election or safe harbor exists in Samoan law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Fa'aputugatupe Tutotonu o Samoa), operating under the Exchange Control Act 1970 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1971
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan tālā (WST) is not fully convertible and is managed under a central bank administered exchange control framework. Current account transactions, including trade payments, service fees, and profit remittances, are generally approved on a documentary basis, but capital account flows require prior Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) authorisation via an authorised dealer. For a Samoa International Company (IC) operating under the International Companies Act 2012, all treasury transactions may be settled in foreign currency (USD, EUR, AUD) without WST conversion, provided the IC maintains non-resident status, does not conduct domestic business with Samoan residents, and does not acquire Samoan land. Profit remittances and dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are free from Samoan withholding tax under the IC tax-exempt regime. However, authorised dealers will typically require an undertaking confirming the beneficiary’s non-resident status, a board resolution, a tax exemption certificate, and a completed Samoa International Transactions Reporting System (ITRS) declaration before processing any outbound WST conversion or cross-border profit transfer. Practical remittance hurdles include enhanced source-of-funds diligence on shareholder injections where the underlying wealth originates from jurisdictions outside the FATF-recognised network, and a possible 48-hour hold on transactions exceeding USD 500,000 pending CBS reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under regulation 17 of the Exchange Control Regulations 1971, all goods exported from Samoa must be paid for through an authorised dealer and the full foreign exchange proceeds must be repatriated to Samoa within 180 days from the date of bill of lading or date of shipment, whichever is later. Unless an exemption is obtained from the Central Bank of Samoa, the mandatory conversion ratio is 100% of the export value into WST on the date the proceeds are received by the authorised dealer. For an International Company engaging in manufacturing resin statues for export, a blanket exemption may be applied for through the authorised dealer to retain 100% of export receipts in a designated USD or EUR retention account, provided the IC exports exclusively through a bonded manufacturing model, maintains no WST operational liabilities, and submits an annual export schedule and external auditor confirmation to the CBS.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Offshore International Company Operating Current Account (USD/EUR/AUD)
Escrow / Operational WST Account requiring CBS non-resident exemption and foreign currency re-designation

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for foreign digital EMI / cross-border payment fintechs such as Airwallex, Ebury, MultiPass, or Currencycloud, provided they operate through an authorised partner bank in a FATF-equivalent jurisdiction. Legal constraints: Samoa does not have a domestic EMI licensing regime, so offshore EMIs cannot provide WST clearing, Samoan domestic settlement, or direct connectivity to the Central Bank of Samoa. An EMI may be used only as a secondary collection rail for Stripe/PayPal pre-order deposits, subject to the EMI maintaining a full anti-money laundering programme, offering segregated client accounts, and, if possible, providing a dedicated IBAN from a European or Hong Kong banking partner. The primary treasury concentration account must remain with a tier-1 Samoan authorised dealer to preserve CBS visibility and avoid unauthorised dealing issues.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and ultimate beneficial owners are not formally required to travel to Samoa for IC account onboarding. ANZ and BSP permit remote opening using a combination of apostilled/certified corporate registers, notarised passport copies, a signed Limited Power of Attorney appointing a licensed Samoan registered agent, and a live video interview conducted by the bank's compliance officer. Pure documentary remote onboarding without any live interview is not accepted for entities controlled by persons resident in non-FATF whitelisted jurisdictions. In all cases, the Samoan registered agent must physically attend the bank at the account opening meeting on behalf of the company and verify the identity of the directors via a notarised certificate of incumbency.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International Company tax-exempt status without substantive local activity or physical premises
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance bundle comprising: current Certificate of Incorporation, Registered Agent Certificate, term lease or service agreement for a Samoan registered office, board minutes for the current financial year, management accounts, audited financial statements, International Companies Act annual return, tax exemption certificate from the Samoa International Financial Authority, and an economic substance self-assessment mapping intellectual property and purchasing/production activities to Samoa.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner or source of funds originating from high-risk or sanction-sensitive jurisdictions (e.g. high-net-worth individuals from mainland China, Hong Kong, or dealer networks)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source of wealth and source of funds package: bank statements for the preceding 12 months, share purchase agreement, audited entity accounts of the parent company, tax records or equivalent wealth declaration, professional reference letter from a licensed lawyer/accountant in the UBO's jurisdiction, police clearance or adverse media search explanation, and a formal beneficial ownership disclosure form naming all shareholders and their economic profile.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pre-order e-commerce deposits received from a large number of consumers or unknown collectors via Stripe/PayPal, creating potential retail money laundering or sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: E-commerce compliance pack: payment processor settlement statements for the last 12 months, order-to-refund reconciliation log, e-commerce platform terms and service agreement, export order register, customer sanctions screening report, IP address geolocation summary, and a written AML policy covering buyer KYC, withdrawal controls, and refund verification for all pre-order deposits above USD 10,000.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity and shareholder loan injections must be routed through the IC's principal USD or EUR treasury account held with an authorised dealer in Samoa. The remitter must effect payment via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 with exact field 72 instructions: /REC/ Equity injection for WS_IC ISIC 3240-05 Resin Statue Garage Kits; /REL/ WS_IC Board Resolution 2026-01. The Bank will require a completed capital confirmation letter, the signed Share Allotment Certificate, a Return of Allotment filing, a beneficial ownership declaration, and the Samoa International Financial Authority tax exemption certificate. For all injections above USD 250,000, the authorised dealer will file the transaction under the ITRS code 'A2 – Equity capital' and may stop suspicious transfers pending specific purpose-code verification. The IC must never route shareholder funds through a third-party personal account, crowdfunding wallet, or crypto exchange because this will trigger automatic enhanced due diligence and potential account suspension.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments to resin compound suppliers, silicone mould fabricators, packaging vendors, freight forwarders, and design contractors should be cleared by debit from the treasury account via SWIFT MT103 directly to the beneficiary bank. For purchase orders exceeding USD 100,000, an unconfirmed at-sight commercial letter of credit (LC MT700) opened through an authorised dealer provides title transfer protection; a standby LC (MT760) can be used to secure pre-order deposits attracted via Stripe/PayPal. The documentary file for each disbursement must retain the commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or airway bill, Certificate of Origin, insurance certificate, and incoterm evidence. Payments to Chinese or Taiwanese resin suppliers travelling through USD clearing hubs (e.g. New York CHIPS) must include clear beneficiary bank identifiers and invoice references; garbled MT103 remittance information will trigger Nostro reconciliation delays and may be rejected by the receiving correspondent.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts with an authorised dealer for USD/EUR, USD/AUD, and USD/WST tenors up to 12 months, backed by verified commercial invoices and requiring a 10% cash margin deposit
Cross-currency swaps between USD and EUR only for matched trade settlement flows, with no embedded leverage and full collateralisation via treasury liquidity balances
Vanilla FX options (call/put on USD/EUR) purchased through the authorised dealer for hedging committed pre-order and raw-material exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the International Company (confirmation of registered office, registered agent, directors, secretary, issued shares and members as prescribed by the International Companies Act 1987, as amended)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies - Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after each anniversary of incorporation; anniversary-based, not calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default is an offence under the Act; the Registrar may impose late filing penalties and publish a Gazette strike-off notice; persistent default leads to administrative dissolution, loss of limited liability capacity, and court-ordered restoration only upon payment of arrears and penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Payment of Annual License Fee (registry retention and renewal) accompanying the Annual Return; no separate franchise or capital-based annual tax is levied
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable on or before the anniversary of incorporation, remitted through the licensed registered agent; should be settled within the Annual Return filing window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues penalty per the International Companies (Fees) Regulations; non-payment beyond 60 days from the anniversary triggers a Gazette strike-off notice; continued default leads to administrative strike-off without court order, after which the company cannot transact and directors may be personally liable for post-dissolution trading

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AML/CFT Client Due Diligence Refresh and Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (no public UBO return is filed in Samoa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed International Company Registered Agent (AML/CFT supervision by SIFA and the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit under the AML/CFT Act 2007, as amended)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once every 12 months, coordinated with the annual renewal cycle, and immediately upon any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Breach triggers administrative fines, AML/CFT supervisory directives, and possible suspension of the registered agent's licence; it does not directly dissolve the company but blocks agent certification and all subsequent registry filings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is compulsory for a Samoa International Company: the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) exempts ICs from audit and from filing financial statements. An audit becomes mandatory only if (a) the articles of association require it, (b) the company's shares are listed on a recognised stock exchange, (c) shareholders holding at least 10% of issued capital request an audit, or (d) a court or the Registrar so directs.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No prescribed filing framework and no requirement to prepare statutory financial statements. Voluntarily prepared accounts should present a true and fair view and may follow IFRS, IFRS for SMEs, or Samoa Local GAAP at the board's discretion; books may be maintained in Samoa Tala or any foreign currency and must sufficiently explain transactions and financial position.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Samoa maintains no public beneficial ownership registry and imposes no recurring UBO filing to the Government. The registered agent holds the confidential register of shareholders and beneficial owners under the AML/CFT regime; the annual KYC refresh, completed at each renewal and within 14 days of any share transfer, together with the updated Register of Members, operates as the company's annual confirmation of ownership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Mortgages and Charges (if any)
Minute Book of board and shareholder resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - 1,200 per annum (market range for licensed Samoa registered agent, registered office, and base AML/KYC compliance service)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 for compulsory statutory audit (exempt); voluntary audit or agreed-upon procedures for payment-processor or bank due diligence, if commissioned, approximately USD 1,800 - 4,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% effective statutory rate for the International Company (Tax-Exempt Zone) under the International Companies Act 1987; the general resident corporate headline rate is 27% under the Income Tax Ordinance 2015, which does not apply to the IC
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Complete statutory tax exemption for International Companies: no income tax, no capital gains tax, no dividend withholding tax on distributions to non-residents, and no estate or transfer duty on share transfers; the exemption is confirmed by a consolidated exemption clause in Part VI of the International Companies Act 1987 and requires no application for a tax holiday

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (Form IC-AR prescribed under Part VI of the International Companies Act 1987), filed via the licensed Registered Agent through the Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) Corporate Registry and electronic company register; no Samoa income tax return is required because the IC is statutorily tax-exempt
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (calendar-year basis; an IC may adopt an alternate financial year-end by notice to the Registrar)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Return and Annual License Fee renewal are due on or before the last day of the month immediately following the anniversary of incorporation; a 30-day grace period is available at the Registrar's discretion, after which late penalties accrue

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the International Company, incorporation number, and date of incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation; any change must be effected by special resolution and filed with the Registrar before the annual return is submitted

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address in Samoa (physical street address, not a P.O. Box alone)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered office must be the office of the licensed Registered Agent in Apia; a non-resident owner may not designate a foreign address

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered Agent name, license number, and contact details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the licensed agent appointed upon incorporation remains in office; if the non-resident owner changes agents, provide a signed statement of consent from the incoming agent

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full particulars of directors and secretary (names, nationalities, residential addresses, passport or ID numbers)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may serve as directors; at least one officer with local presence is recommended; attach certified passport copies and proof of residential address for each officer

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholder register summary: name, nationality, address, class and number of shares held, and beneficial owner declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a 100% non-resident-owned IC, disclose each ultimate beneficial owner; bearer shares are prohibited; attach a signed beneficial ownership declaration for the AML file

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual compliance declaration: no domestic Samoa trading, no contravention of the International Companies Act, and maintained accounting records
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declaration must be signed by a director; a false declaration is a criminal offence and will expose the IC to loss of tax exemption and deregistration

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual License Fee computation and payment confirmation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The fee is based on authorised capital; pay via the Registered Agent together with the government filing fee and retain the Registrar's receipt as proof of good standing

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of WST 500 per month or part thereof up to a maximum of WST 5,000; late license fee payment carries a 10% late-payment surcharge plus a daily surcharge of 0.2% per day until settlement; continued non-compliance beyond 6 months triggers compulsory strike-off and dissolution, forfeiture of the IC's assets to the Crown, and director disqualification

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions made by a Samoa International Company (statutory override in the International Companies Act 1987); Samoa's general non-resident dividend withholding tax is 15% under the Income Tax Ordinance 2015, but it does not apply to an exempt IC
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No withholding tax arises on IC distributions, so no treaty relief claim is required at the Samoan source. For any residual payment subject to Samoa resident-company WHT, the non-resident payee must: (1) obtain an annual Samoa Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Samoa Ministry for Revenue, (2) submit the TRC together with the applicable WHT declaration form to the payer before payment, and (3) rely on the relevant Double Taxation Arrangement (principally Australia and New Zealand) for a reduced or nil rate. IC shareholders should instead obtain a director's resolution confirming the statutory exemption and attach it to bank payment instructions
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Samoa WHT on royalties and interest paid by a resident company to non-residents is 15% each; treaty-reduced rates are available under Samoa's DTA network (e.g., Australia and New Zealand) upon TRC submission. An International Company is exempt from these WHT obligations on both royalty and interest payments made to non-residents, provided the payments relate to its offshore business and are not attributable to a Samoa domestic trade

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa has no codified Local File/Master File monetary threshold in the Income Tax Ordinance; International Companies are outside the income tax net and are not statutorily required to maintain TP documentation. As best-practice governance for the resin statue business, maintain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File and Master File) where connected-party transactions exceed WST 1,000,000 per annum or where the IC invoices related-party sales of polyresin statues
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa applies economic substance expectations to International Companies under the International Companies Act 1987 and administrative guidance aligned with the EU Code of Conduct Group criteria. The IC must demonstrate: a physical registered office in Samoa, a licensed resident Registered Agent, adequate local books and records, board meetings or written resolutions for decision-making regarding the resin statue distribution business, and core income-generating activities conducted in Samoa relative to the entity's role. A pure 'mailbox' IC without substance risks recharacterisation, loss of the tax exemption, and listing-related sanctions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Samoa International Company to sell resin statues or accept pre-order deposits from Samoa resident customers, or carrying on the manufacturing and sales business from a Samoa physical location, which is prohibited by the International Companies Act 1987 and converts the IC into a taxable resident company under the Income Tax Ordinance 2015
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive imposition of 27% corporate income tax on all income derived since the prohibited trading began, plus late payment penalties of 10% and a daily surcharge of 0.2%; fines not exceeding WST 10,000 under the International Companies Act; compulsory deregistration of the IC
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the resulting tax and penalties; the corporate veil is pierced for fraudulent trading, leading to civil restitution orders, disqualification from acting as a director for up to 10 years, travel bans, and imprisonment not exceeding 5 years

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a brass-plate shell with no physical presence, no local registered agent engagement, no Samoa accounting records, and no board oversight of the actual resin statue manufacturing and sale operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Blacklisting by the EU and Samoa's financial services regulator; loss of the IC's Tax-Exempt Zone status with retroactive tax assessments; fines up to WST 50,000; freeze of bank accounts connected to the entity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for debts incurred while the IC was acting in violation of the economic substance expectations; disqualification orders and prohibition from reincorporation in Samoa; asset tracing and civil recovery proceedings

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Stripe and PayPal pre-order deposits and payments into the IC's bank account without conducting customer due diligence, beneficial ownership verification, or sanctions screening, contrary to Samoa's Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2018
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fines up to WST 1,000,000 for the corporate entity; confiscation of transaction funds under the Proceeds of Crime Act; revocation of the Registered Agent's license; the entity may be struck off as an unacceptable financial vehicle
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and ultimate beneficial owners face criminal prosecution with imprisonment up to 14 years, personal fines, forfeiture of personal assets, and international travel bans pending investigation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing resin statue sales to the IC at artificial low margins or transferring intangibles to the Samoa IC without payment or substance, combined with high-margin resales to end customers, so that profits in the manufacturing jurisdiction are stranded in a tax-exempt shell
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment of the taxable base in counterparty jurisdictions with an associated 20% penalty on the additional tax and back-dated interest; the Samoa IC loses its exemption if the arrangement is found to be an abusive shell; global anti-avoidance measures may deny treaty and exemption benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved the sham documentation are jointly liable for the penalty tax; cross-border cooperation (ATO, IRD, OECD exchange of information) can expose them to personal recovery actions and criminal indictment for tax fraud
